Class ResourceWaiter<T>

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.core.waiter.ResourceWaiter<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the resource type
public final class ResourceWaiter<T> extends Object
A small, generic poller for asynchronous Equinix resources: re-fetch a resource on an interval until it reaches a desired state, fails, or a timeout elapses. Most provisioning operations are asynchronous (a created connection starts PROVISIONING and later becomes PROVISIONED); this removes the hand-rolled sleep/poll loops callers would otherwise write.

Usage

Connection conn = fabric.connections().define(ConnectionType.EVPL_VC)... .create();

Connection ready = ResourceWaiter.forResource(() -> fabric.connections().getByUuid(conn.getUuid()))
        .until(c -> c.getState() == ConnectionState.PROVISIONED)
        .failWhen(c -> c.getState() == ConnectionState.FAILED)
        .timeout(Duration.ofMinutes(10))
        .pollInterval(Duration.ofSeconds(15))
        .await();

await() returns the resource once the success condition holds, throws WaiterFailedException if the failure condition is reached first, and WaiterTimeoutException if neither happens before the timeout.

    • await

      public T await()
      Polls until the success condition holds (returning the resource), the failure condition holds (WaiterFailedException), or the timeout elapses (WaiterTimeoutException). Each sleep is clamped to the remaining timeout budget, so the total wait never exceeds the configured timeout by more than one final fetch.

      If the polling thread is interrupted while sleeping, a plain WaiterException is thrown and the thread's interrupt flag is restored.

      Returns:
      the resource once the success condition is met
